artboards.title: The paper — what a document looks like
The trace — how the agent got there

annotations.text:
Every screen has working controls — click before you judge:

· Document — fold the tool steps open, and Resolve flips the thread
· All comments — the filter chips actually filter, counts and all
· The selection panel — switch the two tabs, then press Ask
· Graph — pick a row under MOST REFERENCED to select its node
· Apply — show the diff, then OK for the re-anchor result

Drawn at 1440×900 — a realistic default window, not the wide one on this machine.

The column widths are REX's own: explorer 272, comments 384, both still splittered.

The comment list is the WORKSPACE's now, not the open document's.

So every row names the documents it is about, a comment about two files is one row seen from either of them, and a row can have no gutter marker at all — its places are somewhere else.

Both boards on the right used to carry a floating NEW COMMENT card over the document. It is gone.

The chips, the strength meter and “a region of it” moved onto the selection-panel row, where they still work after the document has been reloaded — the chain is rebuilt from the row's stored anchor, never remembered.

The other half of the palette.

REX's chrome is dark and lives in the renderer. The paper is written by the Markdown renderer in main, and the highlights painted on it by the resolver in the renderer. Both read src/shared/tokens.ts, so a highlight can never drift out of contrast with the page it sits on.

PROPOSED, NOT BUILT — four things on this page.

1. The sidebar's Selection / Comments tabs, on every screen that shows the comments column.

2. “Pick element” left the top bar for the foot of the paper. Keys unchanged: P toggles, hold ⌥. ctrl cannot be that key — on macOS ctrl-click IS a right-click.

3. “go to ›” on a comment card, and its numbered place rows.

4. The trace. The sidebar keeps the conversation and grows a meta strip and a step strip; the machinery moves to a sheet over the document pane, where a bash line and a path can be read. Thinking is drawn there and nowhere else.

None of the four needs new plumbing — and the trace needs no new DATA either: cost, duration, tokens, the profile and the thinking messages are all stored already and simply never drawn.

Why the trace is not in the sidebar.

384px cannot hold a bash line, a path or a diff without wrapping it into mush — which is exactly what Vex's per-tool renderers exist to avoid.

And why it does not replace the document either: an answer is ABOUT a passage, so the answer stays beside it. Only the machinery leaves, because the machinery has nothing to do with the document being on screen.

REX's own rule, one step further: the answer outranks the machinery.
